### cavity2d {#sec-example-laminar-cavity2d}

This example illustrates a flow in a cuboid, lid-driven cavity.
The 2D version also shows how to use the XML parameter files and has an example description file for OpenGPI.
This example is available in two different versions for sequential and parallel use.
The [[`laminar/cavity2dSolver`](/examples/laminar/cavity2dSolver/cavity2dSolver.qmd)]{.content-visible when-format="html"}[`laminar/cavity2dSolver` (@sec-example-laminar-cavity2dSolver)]{.content-visible when-format="pdf"} version illustrates the use of the solver class concept together with the XML parameter interface.


#### Governing equations

The domain $\Omega \times \I \subseteq [0,1]^2 \times \R_{\geq 0}$ is considered with the following governing equations with the velocity field $\vel \in \R^2$ and the pressure $p \in \R$ for the incompressible flow of a Newtonian fluid with kinematic viscosity $\nu \in \R_{> 0}$ and constant density $\rho \in \R_{> 0}$,
\begin{align}
    \nabla \cdot \vel &= 0 \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I, \\
    \partial_t \vel + (\vel \cdot \nabla) \vel &= -\frac{1}{\rho} \nabla p + \nu \Delta \vel \quad \text{in} \quad \Omega \times \I.
\end{align}

#### Boundary conditions

The boundary $\partial \Omega = \Gamma_D \cup \Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$ consists of two parts (@fig-cavity2d-domain): the moving lid $\Gamma_D$ at the top, where the lid velocity is prescribed as a Dirichlet condition, and the three walls at rest $\Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$, where the fluid sticks to the wall,
\begin{align}
    \vel &= (u_\text{lid}, 0)^\top \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_D \times \I, \\
    \vel &= \mathbf{0} \quad \text{on} \quad \Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}} \times \I.
\end{align}
The fluid is initially at rest, $\vel = \mathbf{0}$ in $\Omega$ at $t = 0$.
In `prepareGeometry()`, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{no\text{-}slip}}$ gets the material number 2 and $\Gamma_D$ the material number 3.

#### Domain

The fluid fills a square cavity of side length $L = 1\,\mathrm{m}$ (@fig-cavity2d-domain).
The lid at the top moves with $u_\text{lid} = 1\,\mathrm{m/s}$ in $x$-direction, while the remaining three walls are at rest.
With $\nu = 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$ this gives a Reynolds number of $Re = u_\text{lid} L / \nu = 1000$.

![Domain and boundary conditions of `cavity2d`, with the material numbers (MN) assigned in `prepareGeometry()`.](/examples/laminar/cavity2d/doc/fig/cavity2dDomain.svg){width="60%" #fig-cavity2d-domain .lightbox}

#### Discretization \& Descriptor
In this example, the domain is discretized with a uniform grid of $N^2$ cells with the lattice spacing $\Delta x = L / N$, where $N = 128$ is set by `Resolution` in `cavity2d.xml`.

The LBM collision operator is the BGK operator with a single relaxation time ([Collision Operators](/content/02_core.qmd#collision-operators)), used as `ConstRhoBGKdynamics`, together with the D2Q9 velocity set ([Lattice Structures](/content/01_introduction.qmd#sec-lattice-structures)).
All four walls, including the moving lid, are velocity boundaries of the type `InterpolatedVelocity` ([Define Boundary Method](/content/06_initial_boundary.qmd#sec-defineBoundaryMethod)). The corresponding lattice is defined inside the case definition in 'cavity2d.cpp' as in @lst-cavity2d-case.

::: {#lst-cavity2d-case}
```{.cpp}
using MyCase = Case<
  NavierStokes, Lattice<double, descriptors::D2Q9<>>
>;
```
Case definition for the `cavity2d` example.
:::

The parameters for the simulation are read from `cavity2d.xml` and given in @tbl-cavity2d-params.
The unit converter `UnitConverterFromResolutionAndRelaxationTime` derives the time step size from the resolution and the lattice relaxation time.

| XML element | Symbol | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Discretization/Resolution` | $N$ | $128$ | cells per side length $L$ |
| `Discretization/LatticeRelaxationTime` | $\tau$ | $0.5384$ | lattice relaxation time |
| `PhysParameters/CharPhysLength` | $L$ | $1\,\mathrm{m}$ | side length of the cavity |
| `PhysParameters/CharPhysVelocity` | $u_\text{lid}$ | $1\,\mathrm{m/s}$ | velocity of the lid |
| `PhysParameters/PhysViscosity` | $\nu$ | $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$ | kinematic viscosity |
| `PhysParameters/PhysDensity` | $\rho$ | $1\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}$ | density |
| `PhysParameters/PhysMaxTime` | $T$ | $100\,\mathrm{s}$ | upper limit of the simulated time |
| `ConvergenceCheck/Interval` | | $1\,\mathrm{s}$ | time window of the convergence check |
| `ConvergenceCheck/Residuum` | | $10^{-3}$ | bound for the relative standard deviation of the average energy |
| `Log/SaveTime` | | $1\,\mathrm{s}$ | interval of the console statistics |
| `VisualizationVTK/SaveTime` | | $1\,\mathrm{s}$ | interval of the VTK output |
| `VisualizationImages/SaveTime` | | $5\,\mathrm{s}$ | interval of the velocity heat maps |
| `VisualizationGnuplot/SaveTime` | | $5\,\mathrm{s}$ | interval of the comparison with Ghia et al. |

: Parameters of `cavity2d`, read from `cavity2d.xml` in `main()`. The first seven elements are found below `Param/Application`, the others below `Param/Output`. {#tbl-cavity2d-params}

#### Validation

The velocity and the pressure are written in physical units every second (@fig-example-cavity).

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
![Magnitude of the physical velocity of `cavity2d` from $t = 1\,\mathrm{s}$ until convergence at $t = 28.9\,\mathrm{s}$, visualized in ParaView. The vortex starts in the upper right corner below the lid and moves towards the center of the cavity.](/examples/laminar/cavity2d/doc/fig/cavity2d_velocity.gif){width="100%" #fig-example-cavity .lightbox}
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
![Magnitude of the physical velocity of `cavity2d` at convergence, $t = 28.9\,\mathrm{s}$, visualized in ParaView.](/examples/laminar/cavity2d/doc/fig/cavity2d_velocity_converged.png){width="100%" #fig-example-cavity .lightbox}
:::

The example is validated against the benchmark solution of @GHIA1982387 for $Re = 1000$.
Every $5\,\mathrm{s}$, `getResults()` interpolates the horizontal velocity $u_x$ on the vertical centreline $x = L/2$ at the 17 heights listed in Table I of @GHIA1982387 and writes it together with the reference values to `tmp/gnuplotData/`.
The simulation stops as soon as the steady state is reached. This state is identified via the relative standard deviation of the average energy over the last $1\,\mathrm{s}$. When it falls below $10^{-3}$, which happens at $t \approx 28.9\,\mathrm{s}$ ($iT = 37004$), the simulation is considered converged.
@fig-cavity2d-ghia shows how the profile approaches the reference: the relative $L^2$ error over the 17 points drops from $43\,\%$ at $t = 5\,\mathrm{s}$ to $3.5\,\%$ at convergence.
The example prints this error to the console as `relativeErrorL2(line)`.

#### Files

```
cavity2d/
├── cavity2d.cpp               main(): reads cavity2d.xml; mesh, geometry, lattice, time loop, output and comparison with Ghia et al.
├── cavity2d.xml               parameters of the simulation and of the output
├── description_cavity2d.xml   description of the parameters for OpenGPI
└── Makefile
```

The results are written to `tmp/` in the directory the example is run from. `vtkData/cavity2dvtk.pvd` opens all time steps in ParaView, `imageData/` holds the velocity heat maps and `gnuplotData/` the comparisons with Ghia et al. as plots and data.
